## Findings ledger
- [D3.DOC7.F5] Riley adds uneven development as a necessary explanatory theme linking industrial advancement, agrarian inefficiency and imperial pressure — dim: theme_position — anchor: "gdp per capita does not account adequately for one of the central features of the German prewar economy: its unevenness" — doc: em:VF5R7DTE — anchor-b: "Germany was both ‘Europe’s most advanced industrial and capitalist society’ and ‘an old regime’." — doc-b: em:VF5R7DTE — reader: Dylan Riley — theme-origin: reader_addition — theme: Uneven development — plan-theme-link: outside-spine — position: Riley argues that uneven development, rather than aggregate income or a linear modernization scale, explains how advanced industry coexisted with inefficient agriculture and pressures toward external expansion — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor: yes

scope_outcomes.criterion: The citing author’s text must substantively interpret at least one supplied engagement theme or introduce and substantively support a related reader theme.
scope_outcomes.basis: The complete supplied article substantively addresses estates and social closure, imperialism and economic competition, the historical applicability of estate-related categories, and Weberian rationality; it also introduces uneven development as an explanatory theme.
limitations: This is one 2014 article and not Riley’s complete work or Weber’s entire reception.
The article does not directly address patrimonialism, tax-farming, or political capitalism as a named concept.
No claims about citation frequency or reader ranking are made.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
blocking_issues: Findings lost anchor evidence; this does not establish absence
One or more declared finding references lack retained verified evidence
